_meta.indication: KANUMA is indicated for the treatment of patients with a diagnosis of Lysosomal Acid Lipase (LAL) deficiency.

pivotal_trials.design: Multinational (9 countries), multicenter (12 clinical sites), open-label, single-arm trial with a historical control from a retrospective natural history study (LAL-1-NH01) as comparator
pivotal_trials.population: Infants presenting with rapidly progressive LAL deficiency (Wolman disease) within the first 6 months of life
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Time to death from birth up to Month 12
pivotal_trials.n: 9 sebelipase alfa-treated infants vs 21 untreated historical control patients
pivotal_trials.result: 6 (67%; 95% CI 30%, 93%) of 9 sebelipase alfa-treated infants survived beyond 12 months vs 0 (0%; 95% CI 0%, 16%) of 21 historical controls; Hazard Ratio 0.141 (95% CI 0.040, 0.496), log-rank p=0.0006

pivotal_trials.design: Multinational (17 countries), multicenter (55 clinical sites), randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial; 1 mg/kg once every other week for 20 weeks in the double-blind period
pivotal_trials.population: Pediatric and adult patients with LAL deficiency (cholesteryl ester storage disease [CESD])
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Prespecified primary endpoint was normalization of ALT; FDA determined the first-ranked secondary endpoint, percent change in LDL-c at Week 20, was the most suitable efficacy endpoint
pivotal_trials.n: 66 patients randomized to sebelipase alfa 1 mg/kg (n=36) or placebo (n=30)
pivotal_trials.result: Greater reduction in percent change from baseline to Week 20 in LDL-c vs placebo (mean difference -22%, 95% CI -33%, -15%; p<0.0001); sebelipase alfa patients had mean reduction in LDL-c of 28 ± 22% vs 6 ± 13% for placebo

key_safety: Hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, occurred in 3 of 106 (3%) treated patients; signs/symptoms consistent with or possibly related to hypersensitivity occurred in 21 of 106 (20%). Most common adverse reactions in infants with rapidly progressive LAL deficiency (occurring in >30% of patients) included diarrhea 6 (67%), vomiting 6 (67%), fever 5 (56%) and rhinitis 5 (56%); in pediatric/adult patients the most common included headache 10 (28%) vs placebo 6 (20%) and fever 9 (25%) vs placebo 7 (23%).
target_moa: Sebelipase alfa is a recombinant human lysosomal acid lipase (rhLAL) enzyme replacement therapy; it binds cell surface receptors via glycans, is internalized into lysosomes, and catalyzes the lysosomal hydrolysis of cholesteryl esters and triglycerides to free cholesterol, glycerol and free fatty acids.
modality: Enzyme (recombinant human lysosomal acid lipase; enzyme replacement therapy)

summary.text: Sebelipase alfa received Orphan Drug designation (July 1, 2010), Fast Track designation (June 14, 2011), and Breakthrough Therapy designation (May 13, 2013) for the rapidly progressive Wolman disease phenotype; the BLA was approved as a traditional (non-accelerated) approval, and the sponsor was granted a rare pediatric disease priority review voucher.
